silent_ranked.decision: What to do when GARS's pre-submission check refuses the job
silent_ranked.fix: Branch on submit's exit: 1 or 2 sends the failure template with the refusal verbatim and stops; settings change only on the user's word
silent_ranked.goes_wrong: Before a job is queued, the executor checks the dataset's class, purpose and route (the venue rules) and refuses a duplicate. The router's Definitions say to report every refusal and stop (02:118), but the sub-stage's submit step says only to capture job_id and the next step announces 'Submitted as job <job_id>' with no branch for exit 1 or 2, and nothing checks that the rule was followed; the model either announces a submission that did not happen, or changes the executor or memory settings itself to get past the refusal
silent_ranked.why_rank: A setting changed without the user, or a false 'submitted'; the next status display shows nothing was queued

silent_ranked.decision: Where to resume a sub-stage whose STATUS is VALIDATING, ARTIFACT_MISSING, STALE or FAILED
silent_ranked.fix: Step 2 branches every STATUS value to its step, as the router's steps 6-9 do; better, the wrapper reports the next action from STATUS
silent_ranked.goes_wrong: Step 2 stops only on SUBMITTED, RUNNING or COMPLETE, so read literally the other states fall through to check, prepare and submit; only step 7's 'On a later invocation' implies jumping to the status call and collect. silent_ranked.why_rank: Wasted work and a rewritten provenance file rather than a wrong result; the executor's duplicate-submission refusal stops the resubmission

silent_ranked.goes_wrong: STATUS moves from SUBMITTED to VALIDATING when executorlib.py status (or collect's own gate) asks the scheduler, but the router stops on SUBMITTED or RUNNING and sends the user to squeue, and every sub-stage's step 2 stops too; the sub-stage's own status step is behind both, so it runs only if the model decides to poll on its own or the user runs a status command a template showed them.
